claim: For arbitrary finite labelled alphabets, finite declared point/context/color arrays and word lengths, a single actual native WG P/E constructor computes the word-sum lookup or a proof-of-absence refusal, retaining the request, input-family and program histories; variable-word substitution gives the declared base plus positive repeated-letter sum on the same source policy. The signed three-integer geometry laws are constructed, not postulated. This is relative to the supplied point/context arrays, not a theorem of uniform sector-context realization or complete L_N input admission.
formal_quantifiers: All k,m,n,r and all finite pattern, point, context and color functions. Requests have length-indexed finite-word types. No region index is an input parameter of the query. No monochromatic witness enters the seed policy.
refusal: Exhaustive finite equality search constructs a proof that every supplied point differs from Phi(w). A native E over that proof space retains the certificate; its premises use a zero-arity native P derivation, not a fabricated refusal seed.
substitution: Prove by induction for arbitrary templates in a discrete commutative monoid, instantiate all signed integer triples, and prove a nonempty variable mask has positive multiplicity. Preserve the same typed initial family; do not infer whole-package equivalence from scalar equality.
strongest_rival: The relative native program still typechecks if a genuine sector context at the origin is deliberately assigned a different declared point. Its relative lookup theorem cannot prove the missing point/context binding. The external source-binding check must reject that instance, and the full uniform task-package conjecture must remain open.
controls: false refusal for an in-region point
misbound actual sector context passes relative native typing but fails source binding
stop_condition: Record the quantified relative constructor and exact remaining witnesses on the existing uniform conjecture. Do not silently assume a uniformly realized complete L_N family, upgrade opaque-context soundness to source admission, or add another fixed-cutoff conjecture.
